title: Listing credentials and OAuth flow checklist + tile copy drafts
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working micro-playbook to land partner credentials (OAuth / API keys) for cloud marketplace listings and to draft short tile copy variations that match our compliance and entitlements model. Intended audience: GTM, partner engineering, partner ops, and listing reviewers.

Scope:
- Scope includes SaaS partners and ISVs listing Redwood-hosted connectors and private deployments that require token exchange or delegated access.
- Covers: tile copy (short/long), entitlement metadata, OAuth app registration checklist, token lifecycle requirements, QA smoke tests, and acceptance gates for publishing.

Quick wins / goals:
- Remove last-minute engineering blockers by standardizing required redirect and token behaviors.
- Provide 3 ready-to-use tile copy variants (short tagline, 1-line, 3-bullet) to speed creative sign-off.
- Make a clear pass/fail acceptance checklist that listing reviewers and security can use.

Tile copy drafts (pick one variant per listing):
Variant A – Concise (for catalog card):
  Title: "Connect: {PartnerName} → Redwood"
  Tagline (7–10 words): "Securely route LLM inference to your {partnerFeature}."
  1-line: "Use {PartnerName} with Redwood to keep data local and scale inference."

Variant B – Product-led (for trial pages):
  Title: "{PartnerName} integration for low-latency inference"
  Tagline: "Bring model serving close to your data — fast, audited, and cost-aware."
  Bullets (3):
    - "Dedicated routing and entitlement support for enterprise workloads"
    - "Out-of-the-box SSO + token-based credential exchange"
    - "Usage insights and cost breakdowns per tenant"

Variant C – Compliance-first (for regulated verticals):
  Title: "{PartnerName} (Private / VPC) — Redwood-ready"
  Tagline: "Deploy inference with tenant isolation, HIPAA-friendly controls, and audit logs."
  Bullets (3):
    - "Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit trails"
    - "Configurable data residency and logging retention"
    - "SLA-backed options for dedicated capacity"

Note to copy: {PartnerName} placeholder must be replaced and capitalization verified; avoid word "AI" in regulated verticals alt copy.

OAuth / Credential checklist (required fields and behaviors):
- App registration
  - Partner registers an OAuth client in their console OR we register on their behalf (confirm ownership).
  - Provide explicit redirect URIs to the Redwood partner callback endpoints (env-specific): e.g., https://partners.redwood.ai/oauth/callback (staging/prod).
  - Support exact-match redirect check; avoid wildcard redirect unless security-approved.
- Client types and PKCE
  - If client is public (mobile/web SPA) require PKCE.
  - Confidential clients must have client_secret rotation plan and min length 32 chars.
- Scopes & least privilege
  - Scopes must be explicit and documented. Default minimal scope: read:user_metadata, invoke:inference.
  - No broad scopes like "admin:*" for marketplace onboarding.
- Token lifecycle
  - Access tokens: expiry <= 1 hour for customer-facing integrations; recommend 15m–60m.
  - Refresh tokens: allowed only for confidential apps; require revocation endpoint and rotation.
  - Token introspection endpoint available (if requested by security review).
- Consent/UX
  - Consent screen copy must list what Redwood accesses and how tokens are used (example text included below).
- Security requirements
  - TLS 1.2+ on all endpoints, HSTS, and CORS restricted to known origins.
  - JWK set (JWKS) endpoint for validating signed tokens (if partners sign tokens).
  - Rate limit and abuse protections documented.
- Entitlement metadata
  - partner.entitlement.id (string), partner.entitlement.plan (free|trial|paid), tenant_bound (boolean).
  - Metadata should be returned in the token exchange / provisioning response or available from partner API.

Token exchange example (recommended flow):
1) Partner redirects user -> Redwood OAuth consent to grant inference_invoker scope.
2) Redwood exchanges auth code -> partner token endpoint using client_assertion or client_secret.
3) Partner returns a short-lived access_token + optional tenant_id and entitlement flags in JSON.
4) Redwood stores the access_token encrypted in KMS, caches token with TTL aligned to expiry, and refreshes via partner refresh token if present.

Minimum API behaviors partner must provide:
- POST /token (RFC6749): support grant_type=authorization_code and grant_type=refresh_token
- GET /entitlements?tenant_id=<id> -> returns JSON list of entitlements and plan
- POST /revoke for token revocation (RFC7009)
- Optional: POST /introspect to validate token and expiry

Telemetry & gating tests for listing QA:
- Smoke: complete OAuth flow end-to-end in staging, verify token stored and used against demo inference request.
- Security: verify redirect URIs blocked for invalid origins, require PKCE on public clients.
- Functional: supply entitlement flag that toggles a feature in demo (e.g., higher concurrency) and assert behavior.
- Observability: ensure partner returns request IDs for trace linking and include them in Redwood logs.

Acceptance criteria (pass / fail gates):
- Pass: OAuth flow completes without manual token injection; entitlement metadata present; demo inference succeeds using returned token; tile copy approved by GTM; legal sign-off on data residency statements.
- Fail: Missing revoke endpoint; missing entitlement metadata; redirect URI wildcards without security exception; token expiry > 24h for access tokens.

Operational considerations / notes to SRE/Infra team:
- Token caching: cache per-tenant token TTL = min(access_token_expiry, 30m) by default to reduce token exchange bursts.
- Retry strategy: exponential backoff for token refresh and token-exchange calls (max 3 attempts).
- Fallback policies: if partner token exchange fails, route to fallback model variant and surface a clear error to the application (document error codes).

Mock consent copy (place on the partner consent screen):
- "Redwood Inference will use this permission to request short-term tokens to run models on your behalf. We will not store raw customer content beyond runtime unless you opt-in. Tokens are used to identify and authorize inference requests; you can revoke access anytime."

Stakeholders and owners (first pass):
- Partner integration owner: James Rowe
- Listing copy + GTM approval: Asha Patel
- Security review: Elena García
- Engineering liaison: Priya Sen

Timeline (example sprint):
- Week 0: Kickoff + tech discovery with partner (JIRA-4231)
- Week 1: App registration + redirect URI verification + initial tile copy drafted
- Week 2: Staging OAuth smoke + entitlements wiring + security checklist sign-off
- Week 3: Final tile copy and creative (marketing) + publishing readiness review

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we require token introspection on all partners or only on enterprise partners? (security input needed)
- Should we mandate JWKS for signed tokens, or accept opaque tokens with introspection endpoint only?
- Add example curl snippets for token exchange (engineering to draft).

Next steps (short):
- Assign a JIRA to capture partner-specific redirect URIs and env variables (JIRA-4231 exists).
- Engineering: add a small e2e smoke harness that uses the partner staging token endpoint.
- GTM: choose one tile variant and produce final copy for the listing.

Notes to self: keep copy short—marketplace tiles are scanned by search and need primary keywords in first 6 words. Also keep a variant that explicitly calls out "Private / VPC" when the partner integration supports it.

References:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GM/marketplace-onboarding-playbook
- Security checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/OAuth+Integration+Guidelines

-- end of draft --
